title: Legislative districts of Iloilo City
wikitext:
{{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Iloilo City''' are the representations of the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] of [[Iloilo City|Iloilo]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The city is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. == History == The territory of what is now Iloilo City initially formed part of the [[Legislative districts of Iloilo#1907–1972|second district]] of [[Iloilo province]] in 1907. At the time of the passage of the Election Law (Act No. 1582) for the [[Philippine Legislature]] on January 9, 1907,{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/stream/actsphilippinec02unkngoog#page/n110/mode/2up|title=Acts of the Philippine Commission, No. 1-1800 - Volume X|publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office|place=Washington, D.C.|author=United States Department of War|year=1901 }} [[Arevalo, Iloilo City|Arevalo]] was a separate municipality, while the municipality of Iloilo was, by virtue of Act No. 719 of April 3, 1903, composed of the territories of the Spanish-era ''pueblos'' of [[Iloilo City Proper|Iloilo]], [[Jaro, Iloilo City|Jaro]], [[La Paz, Iloilo City|La Paz]], [[Mandurriao]] and [[Molo, Iloilo City|Molo]]. Jaro once again became a separate municipality by virtue of Executive Order No. 64 issued on December 24, 1907, while La Paz was re-established in 1920 by virtue of Executive Order No. 70 signed on October 11, 1919. When seats for the [[Senate of the Philippines|upper house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] were elected from territory-based districts between 1916 and 1935, the then-municipalities of Arevalo, Iloilo (also encompassing Mandurriao and Molo), Jaro and La Paz — along with the rest of [[Iloilo province]] — formed part of the [[Senatorial districts of the Philippines#Seventh District|seventh senatorial district]] which elected two out of the 24-member senate. When the City of Iloilo was created in 1936 by merging the municipalities of Arevalo, Iloilo and La Paz, the new city remained within the [[Legislative districts of Iloilo#1907–1972|second district of Iloilo province]]. Jaro, also part of the second district, was annexed to the city later in 1940. In the disruption caused by the [[Second World War]], [[#1943–1944|two delegates]] represented the chartered city ([[Legislative districts of Iloilo#1943–1944|separately from the province]]) in the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the city mayor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through an assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members within the city during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, the city's representation reverted to the [[Legislative districts of Iloilo#1907–1972|second district of Iloilo province]], of which it remained a part until 1972. Iloilo City was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region VI]] from 1978 to 1984. The city, along with the rest of the province of Iloilo, elected [[Legislative districts of Iloilo#1984–1986|five representatives, at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in the [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984 elections]]. Iloilo City was provided its own [[House of Representatives of the Philippines#District representation|congressional district]] under the new Constitution{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|access-date=June 13, 2016}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987.
